A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 20 readable pages including Appendices A–D. Complete text and rendered-page comparison establishes that differences are confined to the first-page version/date stamp and presentation edits in Figure 13.

before.justification: v2 reports original localization experiments on PixArt-α, FLUX, and SANA, plus personalization and unlearning evaluations in Sections 3.3 and 4.3. Appendix B includes additional experimental results and analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original quantitative and qualitative localization, personalization, and unlearning results, including the supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The attention-contribution ranking, top-K prompt interventions, and localized personalization and unlearning procedures in Sections 3.2 and 4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six LOCK knowledge categories, personalization and unlearning tasks, and COCO evaluation data. Dataset descriptions, Table 1, and the scenarios illustrated in Figure 13 are retained.

E2.justification: The brute-force localization comparator in Appendix B.2 and full-model fine-tuning comparisons for personalization and unlearning are unchanged. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, model configurations, and training settings match. Both retain K=9 of 28 blocks for personalization, K=5 for unlearning, and the same K values in Figure 13.

E4.justification: The analyses varying K, artistic-style complexity study in Appendix B.3.2, and qualitative cases remain unchanged. Figure 13 masks parts of existing examples without adding or removing an analysis.

E5.justification: The description of averaging attention contributions across seeds and prompts is identical. Statistical reporting in the text and plots is unchanged, with no newly reported run counts, intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, trends, and underlying generated examples match. For example, Appendix B.2 retains the proposed method's CLIP score of 0.2061 and CSD score of 0.7781 at K=6. Figure 13 adds display overlays rather than new experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The attention-contribution definitions in Section 3.2, diffusion and flow formulations in Appendix A.1, and unlearning objectives in Appendix C.2 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, reasoning, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same localization method and dataset contributions, causal-localization claim, and claims about efficient personalization and unlearning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of architectural differences and artistic-style complexity are unchanged. Appendix D retains the limitations concerning selection of K, reliance on external metrics, and the lack of ground-truth localization benchmarks.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 retains the same preprocessing, optimizer settings, model details, and RTX A6000 hardware disclosure. The project-page link and fine-tuning script references are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list are identical. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to prior research changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 25 Nov 2025 to v3 dated 26 Jan 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figure 13 adds blur overlays to SpongeBob at K=0% and 10%, and to the faces in the Lionel Messi and Queen Elizabeth II examples at K=0%. The figure is slightly resized/repositioned, retaining its grid and caption. Other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 exposes identifying details in four Figure 13 panels that v3 blurs, making the qualitative comparison of target identities harder to assess. This is a limited loss of inspectability in supporting evidence; the methods, quantitative results, explanations, and main conclusions remain unchanged.
